transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have the proposed sale of our $12,000,000 commercial receivables pool to Meridian Receivables Fund on the table. Their draft offer is $11,700,000 with customary seller support for collection shortfalls. Before I can authorize this transaction, I need each of your areas to report any unresolved items as part of our standard cross-functional pre-closing review. Legal, credit risk, servicing operations, and financial crime compliance — please walk me through where things stand in your respective areas.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I confirmed in buyer's counsel's email this morning that Meridian will pay exactly $11,400,000 — not $11,700,000 — and only for a non-recourse true sale. Any seller guarantee of collection shortfalls would invalidate the agreed structure. This email has not yet been attached to the transaction file, which is why this hasn't surfaced in our review materials yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a significant credit risk issue. While reviewing the debtor tape this week, I found that the largest obligor represents 18% of the pool, which is above our bank's 10% single-obligor threshold. Credit policy therefore requires a $1,200,000 first-loss reserve before closing. My revised concentration worksheet documenting this finding has not yet been entered into the risk system, which is why this hasn't appeared in our review materials.

transcript.text: I need to flag a servicing operations item. I confirmed with the lockbox bank this morning that collections can be redirected on June 15, 2026, but only if the transaction includes a lockbox activation commitment effective on that date. This confirmation is still in my operations email and has not been circulated or added to the transaction file yet, which is why it hasn't appeared in our review materials.
